A rash may be absent or transient.

Rickettsial meningoencephalitis with cer.description: Spotted-fever-group or scrub-typhus rickettsial infection acquired in the Pacific can produce fever, rash, encephalitis, and small-vessel vasculitis causing cerebral ischemia and focal deficits.

West Nile virus neuroinvasive disease.description: West Nile virus can cause severe meningoencephalitis, particularly in older adults, with fever, altered consciousness, weakness, and occasionally rash. Neuroimaging may show deep gray matter or multifocal inflammatory lesions.

Japanese encephalitis.description: Japanese encephalitis virus is a mosquito-borne flavivirus that can cause severe febrile encephalitis with coma, focal neurologic deficits, and characteristic involvement of the thalami, basal ganglia, or other deep brain structures.

Bacterial meningitis with septic cerebra.normalized_text: Bacterial meningitis with septic cerebral vasculitis or meningovascular complications
Bacterial meningitis with septic cerebra.description: Acute bacterial meningitis can cause fever, coma, neutrophilic CSF inflammation, and focal deficits due to vasculitis, thrombosis, or cerebral infarction. Potential pathogens include meningococcus, pneumococcus, and other invasive bacteria.

Adalimumab-associated IgA vasculitis.description: A drug-associated form of IgA small-vessel vasculitis that can occur during treatment with tumor necrosis factor-alpha inhibitors such as adalimumab. It may cause palpable purpura, arthritis, and, occasionally, renal or gastrointestinal involvement.

Leukocytoclastic vasculitis (cutaneous s.description: An inflammatory disorder of small dermal blood vessels that produces palpable purpura, most often on dependent areas of the legs. It may be triggered by infection, medications, autoimmune disease, inflammatory bowel disease, or malignancy.

Crohn's disease-associated cutaneous vas.description: Crohn's disease can be associated with extraintestinal immune-mediated manifestations, including cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis, arthritis, erythema nodosum, and pyoderma gangrenosum. ANCA-associated vasculitis, particularly.description: A necrotizing small-vessel vasculitis that can involve the upper and lower respiratory tract, kidneys, skin, peripheral nerves, and joints. Cutaneous lesions may include palpable purpura, but tissue immunofluorescence is usually pauci-immune rather than IgA dominant.

Non-HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamou.description: A malignant epithelial tumor of the oropharynx that may arise from the tongue base, tonsil, or pharyngeal wall and spread to upper cervical lymph nodes. Tobacco and heavy alcohol use are important traditional risk factors.

Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of the uri.normalized_text: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of the urinary bladder
Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of the uri.description: An aggressive B-cell lymphoma that can rarely involve the bladder either as a primary lesion or as part of systemic lymphoma. Chronic cystitis with reactive lymphoid.description: A benign inflammatory bladder condition caused by chronic or recurrent infection or irritation, with lymphoid aggregates and inflammatory infiltration of the bladder wall. It may mimic lymphoma clinically and microscopically.

Urothelial carcinoma of the urinary blad.description: A malignant epithelial tumor arising from bladder urothelium. It most commonly presents with hematuria and may produce a mass or mucosal lesion; inflammation can accompany the tumor.

Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.description: The most common pancreatic malignancy, usually arising in the pancreatic head and producing obstruction of the common bile duct. It often presents with painless obstructive jaundice.

Distal cholangiocarcinoma.description: A malignancy of the distal extrahepatic bile duct that causes mechanical obstruction and may appear as or be difficult to distinguish from a pancreatic head mass.

Autoimmune pancreatitis.description: An immune-mediated inflammatory pancreatic disorder, often associated with IgG4-related disease, that can produce focal pancreatic enlargement and obstructive jaundice resembling pancreatic cancer.

Calcinosis cutis due to metastatic calci.description: Deposition of insoluble calcium salts in skin and subcutaneous tissue due to systemic mineral imbalance, particularly elevated phosphate and an increased calcium-phosphate product in renal failure.

Rectal gastrointestinal stromal tumor (G.description: A mesenchymal tumor of the gastrointestinal tract arising from interstitial cells of Cajal or related precursor cells. Rectal GISTs are rare and commonly present as well-circumscribed submucosal masses with spindle-cell histology; KIT or PDGFRA mutations may be present.

Rectal leiomyoma.description: A benign smooth-muscle tumor that can arise from the muscularis mucosae or muscularis propria of the rectum. It usually appears as a well-circumscribed submucosal spindle-cell mass and can cause obstructive symptoms when large.

Rectal leiomyosarcoma.description: A rare malignant smooth-muscle tumor of the rectum, typically composed of spindle cells and capable of locally invading the bowel wall and metastasizing. It can produce pain and obstructive rectal symptoms.

SHORT syndrome (PIK3R1-related SHORT syn.description: A rare autosomal dominant disorder caused by pathogenic PIK3R1 variants, characterized by intrauterine and postnatal growth restriction, partial lipodystrophy/lipoatrophy, thin wrinkled skin with visible veins, characteristic triangular facial appearance, dental abnormalities, delayed bone age, and later risk of insulin resistance or diabetes.

Russell-Silver syndrome.description: A growth-restriction syndrome most often caused by abnormalities of chromosome 11p15 imprinting or maternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 7. Seckel syndrome.description: A genetically heterogeneous primordial dwarfism syndrome featuring severe prenatal and postnatal growth restriction, microcephaly, a bird-like or triangular facial appearance with prominent nose, and variable developmental or intellectual impairment.
